text:
alisa: FYI cloud billing alert — big jump in hourly spend for GPU fleet starting ~09:10 UTC, looks like a bunch of on-demand instances launched.
devin: saw the alert, digging in. any obvious autoscaler churn logs?
mike: checking `gcloud compute instances list --filter='labels:gpu' --zones us-central1*` — lots of new instances, many are `a2-highgpu-1g` but several are `n1-standard-8` which is weird for the GPU pool.
julia: that matches the nodegroup names — autoscaler split into `gpu-preemptible` and `gpu-fallback` last night after the template change. think fallback group launched on-demand because spot capacity was exhausted.
alisa: correct. cloud-billing-bot shows a spike of ~$4k in 2 hours. majority on on-demand VMs in us-central1 (our commitments are in us-west1). :grimacing:
sre-oncall: quick checklist — (1) are those on-demand nodes tagged to prod cost center? (2) can we scale them down? (3) is there a reservation/commitment mismatch?
devin: (1) yes — `env=prod,team=runtime`. (2) autoscaler reports `scaleUp: required for pending pods` — but those pending pods are mostly batch preprocessing jobs that requested `gpuCount: 0` due to a recent helm chart bug; they were scheduled onto fallback nodes because the GPU-preemptible pool preferred spot and failed.
mike: looks like a deploy two hours ago changed the nodeTemplate in terraform module `gpu-node-pool` from `preemptible=true` to `preemptible` unset. the autoscaler `fallbackToOnDemand: true` is intentional for availability, but the template mismatch made fallback launch non-GPU types.
julia: here is the suspicious terraform diff snippet from the deploy pipeline:
```
module "gpu_node_pool" {
  source = "git::ssh://.../modules/gpu-pool.git//?ref=v2.3.1"
-  instance_type = "a2-highgpu-1g-preemptible"
+  instance_type = "n1-standard-8"
}
```
alisa: ugh — mismatch across environments. That explains both (a) wrong instance family and (b) commitments not applying. Our committed use discounts are for `A2` family in us-west1 so those `n1` instances don't get the discount.
sre-oncall: immediate action: 1) reduce autoscaler max for fallback pool to 0 for non-essential namespaces, 2) cordon + drain non-GPU nodes that are not needed, 3) patch terraform to correct instance_type and roll back the bad release.
devin: I created a short patch branch and opened a rollback PR. Also ran `kubectl get nodes -l pool=fallback -o wide` and started cordoning nodes that have no GPU label.
mike: started draining the cheapest on-demand nodes first. added `--ignore-daemonsets --delete-emptydir-data` to speed drains where safe.
julia: opened a billing ticket with cloud provider to see if some of the recent allocation can be reclassified under preemptible usage — but honestly unlikely since instances launched as on-demand.
cloud-billing-bot: alert acknowledged. Estimated refund/adjustment window: 1-3 business days. Request ID: CB-2026-0931-77.
alisa: medium-term: we need guardrails — autoscaler should not fall back to on-demand for pools where commitments exist, or at least require an approval. also require infra deploy pipeline to validate instance_family + region vs commitments.
sre-oncall: agreed. followups: - add a pre-deploy check in CI: validate terraform variable `instance_type` against allowed list for gpu pools (A2/A100 families only) - make a Grafana alert when on-demand GPU spend exceeds X% of committed capacity - change autoscaler fallback to `preferSpots: true` and `allowFallback: false` for batch namespaces
devin: logging followups: capturing the sequence of events and cost delta. I'll post a short incident runbook in #incidents once the PR merges.
mike: one extra note — our region constraint logic missed a recent CLI override: someone deployed `region=us-central1` manually. need to gate region changes in the console.
julia: I've tagged the affected nodes with `investigation=preemptible-fallback-1842212345` and added their instance IDs to the incident ticket.
alisa: thanks. target to fully remediate (rollback + drain + autoscaler policy) in next 30 minutes, then post-mortem with cost impact and remediation plan.
devin: rolling back now. will update thread when done.
mike: nodes drained and deleted for the obvious offenders. autoscaler max updated.
devin: rollback merged and applied. terraform plan shows instance_type back to `a2-highgpu-1g-preemptible` for the gpu pool. k8s node templates reconciled.
alisa: nice work. action items for postmortem: - stricter CI validation for instance types and regions - autoscaler policy change to avoid fallback where commitments exist - billing alert thresholds and ownership for committed regions - runbook for draining fallbacks quickly
julia: will draft the postmortem and include cost numbers.
sre-oncall: adding this to the weekly infra review and tagging product owners for the batch jobs that forced scale.
cloud-billing-bot: incident CB-2026-0931-77 updated: mitigation in progress. estimated extra spend avoided: ~$3.6k.
alisa: closing loop here once postmortem is in. great quick response everyone :thumbsup:
